laws.title: PUBLIC UTILITIES: Adds to existing law to provide for new large loads (Idaho Code 61-335, New large load and ratepayer protection)

cites.quote: Reported Signed by Governor on April 10, 2026
Session Law Chapter 335
Effective: 07/01/2026

threshold_mw.value: 50 MW: an increase of 50 MW or more in a service entrance's cumulative power requirement in any consecutive 60-month period, under a service contract entered into on or after July 1, 2026

cites.quote: Results in an increase in a cumulative power requirement of such service entrance of fifty (50) megawatts or more in any consecutive sixty (60) month period
Is subject to a service contract with a public utility that was entered into on or after July 1, 2026.

requirements.value: A public utility serves a new large load only under a commission-approved service contract, filed with a no harm test; the commission approves or denies it within 270 days

cites.quote: A public utility shall provide service to a new large load only pursuant to a commission-approved service contract.

Such filing shall include a no harm test ... The commission shall review and approve or deny a new large load service contract within two hundred seventy (270) days of receiving such filing by the public utility.

requirements.value: The new large load funds its full cost of service, including its share of generation, transmission, substation and distribution investments needed only because of it; the commission reviews the contract's rates in each general rate case

cites.quote: The new large load is responsible for funding its full cost of service, including its share of generation, transmission, substation, and distribution infrastructure investments
In each general rate case filed by a public utility, the commission shall review the rates, charges, and cost recovery mechanisms applicable to an approved service contract

requirements.value: Approval is conditioned on financial security, in a form and amount the commission approves, reasonably sufficient to protect the utility and its other customers from stranded or unrecoverable costs

cites.quote: Approval of a service contract shall be conditioned on the new large load furnishing financial security, in a form and amount approved by the commission

requirements.value: A new large load may not change its status by artifice, such as splitting its load among service entrances

cites.quote: A new large load shall not change its status as such by means of artifice

Status 'in effect': the bill page prints the Governor's signature (April 10, 2026) and 'Effective: 07/01/2026'.

laws.title: Relating to large energy use facilities; and declaring an emergency.

cites.quote: Approved by the Governor June 16, 2025
Effective date June 16, 2025
CHAPTER 323

threshold_mw.value: 20 MW: a facility that uses or is able to use 20 MW or more and is primarily engaged in a service under NAICS code 518210

cites.quote: means a facility that uses or is able to use 20 megawatts or more and is primarily engaged in providing a service described under code 518210

requirements.value: The Public Utility Commission provides a separate classification of service with its own tariff schedule for large energy use facilities; the tariff allocates the class's costs to the class, or directly assigns a facility's costs to it, and mitigates the risk of shifting costs to other classes

cites.quote: The Public Utility Commission shall provide for a classification of service under ORS 757.230 for retail electricity consumers that are large energy use facilities.
Allocate the costs of serving the class of retail electricity consumers that are large energy use facilities to the class in a manner that is equal or proportional to the costs of serving the class

requirements.value: The contract with a large energy use facility is for 10 years or longer

cites.quote: Specify the duration of the contract and be for a duration for 10 years or longer

requirements.value: The contract obligates the customer to pay a minimum amount or percentage, set by the commission, based on its projected electricity usage, for the contract's duration

cites.quote: Obligate the retail electricity consumer to pay a minimum amount or percentage, as determined by the commission

requirements.value: The contract may include a charge for excess demand in addition to the tariff schedule

cites.quote: May include a charge for excess demand for the electricity services the electric company is contracted to provide

requirements.value: The commission reports by September 1 of each even-numbered year on load trends from large energy use facilities (repealed January 2, 2035)

cites.quote: No later than September 1 of each even-numbered year, the Public Utility Commission shall submit a report

laws.bill: H. 3309 (Act No. 41 of 2025, South Carolina Energy Security Act)
laws.title: AN ACT TO AMEND THE SOUTH CAROLINA CODE OF LAWS BY ENACTING THE "SOUTH CAROLINA ENERGY SECURITY ACT"
laws.source_title: H 3309, 126th Session (2025-2026), bill page with history and ratified text (A41, R60, H3309)

cites.quote: Governor's Action: May 12, 2025, Signed
Effective date 05/12/25
Act No. 41

threshold_mw.value: 50 MW at one point of delivery for a 'transformational customer' (with 500 new employees, $100,000,000 investment and a Department of Commerce designation); an existing customer above 20 MW contract demand signing a contract of five years or more is a 'qualifying customer'

cites.quote: (a) 50 megawatts at one point of delivery;

an existing commercial or industrial customer with a combined firm and interruptible contract demand greater than 20 megawatts that agrees to a new or extended electric service contract with a term of five years or more

requirements.value: Economic development agreements with qualifying or transformational customers are for a term not exceeding ten years

cites.quote: The agreement with the customer must be for a term not exceeding ten years

requirements.value: Rates for transformational customers may not be lower than 25 percent below the utility's marginal cost (qualifying customers: not below marginal cost); the commission finds measures were taken to avoid cross-customer class subsidization, and decides within sixty days

cites.quote: rates for transformational customers may not be lower than twenty-five percent less than the electrical utility's marginal cost of providing service to the customer
measures have been taken to avoid or reduce cross-customer class-subsidization
The commission must either approve or deny an application pursuant to this section within sixty days.

requirements.value: A qualifying or transformational customer that leaves the state or ends operations during the ten-year contract reimburses the difference between standard rates and the rates it paid

cites.quote: such customer must reimburse the electrical utility and its customers the difference between standard rates and the rates paid during the term of the agreement

laws.notes: Section 36 of Act 41 adds Chapter 43 of Title 58 (economic development project rates and terms). The Act's text read prints no 'data center' or 'large load' term; it is entered because its transformational customer class sets rate floors, a term limit and an exit reimbursement for loads of 50 MW and up. No 2026 South Carolina act was searched for (search budget spent).

threshold_mw.value: 25 MW contracted or measured demand with an anticipated or measured average annual load factor of 75 percent or more (contracted defense facilities excluded)

cites.quote: means a retail electric service customer that has a contracted or measured electric demand of 25 megawatts or greater and an anticipated or measured average annual electric load factor of 75 percent or greater

requirements.value: By January 15, 2027 each Phase I and Phase II Utility petitions for a voluntary demand flexibility program for high energy demand customers; the SCC issues a final order by November 30, 2027 and sets a demand flexibility standard; carbon-emitting generating resources are ineligible

cites.quote: By January 15, 2027, each Phase I and Phase II Utility shall file a petition with the Commission for approval of a voluntary demand flexibility program that applies to high energy demand customers
The Commission shall issue a final order on such petitions no later than November 30, 2027.
provide that carbon-emitting generating resources will be ineligible for participation in the demand flexibility program

requirements.value: By January 1, 2029 each cooperative serving a high energy demand customer establishes a voluntary demand flexibility program

cites.quote: By January 1, 2029, each cooperative that serves one or more high energy demand customers shall establish a voluntary demand flexibility program

requirements.value: Program incentives may not unreasonably shift costs onto other retail customers; they may include procedures for accelerated interconnection of participating customers

cites.quote: without unreasonably shifting or imposing any costs of program participation or administration onto other retail electric service customers of the utility
Such incentives may also include open and transparent procedures for accelerated interconnection to service by participating high energy demand customers
